issues.description: Method getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): return type differs between artifacts. In the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) the method is declared as returning int (UML line showing '+getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): int'). In the template Lecture.java there is an inline comment instructing a double return type for precise calculation ("Return type: double for precise calculation"). The provided solution implementation declares the method as 'public double getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor()'. This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether to implement an int or a double and can cause failing tests or unexpected results if the tests/solution expect a different type than what the student implements.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected return type consistent across all artifacts. Recommended: update the UML and problem text in problem_statement.md to declare getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): double so it matches the template hint and the solution implementation. Concretely, change the UML line '+getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): int' to '+getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): double' and update any descriptive text that mentions int. Alternatively, if an int is truly intended, change the template comment and the solution implementation to return int and document how to handle rounding/truncation. Ensure tests and example code match the chosen type.
